title: Phone over USB: a setting to leave USB phones alone (mgu-uplink 0.7.7, mgu-updater 0.8.32, Store 0.9.30)
body:
Adds a setting to turn off the USB phone uplink. While it is on, a plugged-in phone can't play USB audio and keeps asking "Trust This Computer?".

## Why a phone loses audio and asks for Trust

With nothing ranked above it, mgu-uplink takes every iPhone plugged in, whether Personal Hotspot is on or not:

- It deauthorizes and reauthorizes the phone in sysfs, which takes it from the media daemon.
- It switches the phone to configuration 4 and claims its hotspot interface. While the uplink holds the phone, it is a network device, not a media device, so USB audio from it stops.
- It opens a lockdown session over usbmux, and pairs when the phone doesn't know the unit. An untrusted phone then shows "Trust This Computer?". A phone where Trust was declined is asked again at its next plug-in.

Android phones are only used while USB tethering is on (RNDIS or NCM).

## What it does

**mgu-uplink 0.7.7**
- New setting `usb_phone`: `on` in the shipped conf and when unset. The `usb-phone` request keeps it in `settings_conf`.
- Off, the scan skips the phone kinds (`rndis`, `ncm`, `iphone`). No phone is deauthorized, switched to another configuration, paired or tethered, so the media daemon, iAP2 and wired CarPlay keep it.
- An iPhone take already in progress stops before its next deauthorize.
- A phone link that is running ends at once, the same way an unplug ends it: an iPhone is handed back to the media daemon, an RNDIS phone is sent HALT. The uplink then moves on to the next device.
- Turned on again, a phone is taken at the next scan.
- USB Ethernet adapters, CDC-ECM sticks and Wi-Fi are unaffected. A stick that presents RNDIS or NCM counts as a phone.
- `status.json` reports the setting as `usbPhone`.

**mgu-updater 0.8.32**
- Relays the privileged `{"op":"usb-phone","on":true|false}`, validated like `wifi-5ghz`.
- Passes `usbPhone` into the state's `uplink` when the uplink reports it.

**robertn_store 0.9.30**
- **Preferred connection**: a row in Settings' Access card, below Accounts, built like the Wi-Fi row. It has an icon, the title, the connection tried first (Automatic, Wi-Fi, USB or Phone) and a chevron. It opens the Preferred connection page.
- The row shows under the same condition as the Wi-Fi row: the uplink reports its Wi-Fi, through an updater that passes it. With an older updater or uplink, or one not on `uplink = auto`, neither row shows.
- The Access card shows three rows at once with no scrolling: Wi-Fi, Accounts and Preferred connection. Proxy and Phone access follow below, as in the release, and the focus order is Wi-Fi, Accounts, Preferred connection, Proxy, Phone access.
- To make room, the head unit and version lines move:
  - iDrive 7: down into the card's empty space, at their released size.
  - iDrive 8: into the card's header row, condensed and right-aligned. The versions line runs along the top. The head unit line sits on the ACCESS line, after the longest translation of ACCESS and HEAD UNIT.
  - On both units, Check now and the rows keep their released size and position.
- The Wi-Fi page has no Preferred button, so the Settings row is the one way in. Use Wi-Fi and Scan stay in their released slots, and the third slot is empty.
- **Phone over USB**: a switch below the groups on the Preferred connection page, in all 32 languages ("Preferred connection" is already translated everywhere).
- The switch is hidden when the uplink or updater doesn't report `usbPhone`, so every update order works and no `requires` change is needed. An older Store ignores the field. A newer updater with an older uplink leaves the field out.

Offline renders (`tools/shots.js`), English, the same fixture on both sides. Before is the released Store (robertn_store 0.9.29, built from 8cfae23); there, the Preferred connection page opens from the Wi-Fi page. Compared pixel by pixel across all 51 fixture screens on both units, only Settings' Access card, the Preferred connection page's switch row and the Wi-Fi page's third button slot differ.

## Tests

- mgu-uplink `go test` covers:
  - the setting is persisted;
  - phones are skipped while off, and the iPhone take stops before any sysfs write;
  - a phone link is released when the switch goes off, and sticks and adapters keep running;
  - phones are picked up again when it goes back on;
  - the ctl request and `status.json`.
- mgu-updater: relay, validation and state tests.
- Store: test_i18n, test_fit, test_screens (including the Access card's first view, focus order and scrolling on every unit), test_store (iD7 and iD8), and the other tools/test_* suites.
- Emulator (iD7), each starting from the published release, with the branch's catalog on a USB stick:
  - each component updated alone: mgu-uplink, mgu-updater, then the Store. After each, the updater runs and stays online, the Store opens, and the rest updates from it.
  - all three updated, with `uplink = auto`: the switch shows, and a tap turns `usb_phone` off in `settings_conf` and in `status.json`; the setting is kept across an uplink restart.
- Store emu-gate passed (`release/gate/robertn_store.json`).

title: iPhone tethering switch: leave a plugged-in iPhone to the car (mgu-uplink 0.7.7, mgu-updater 0.8.32, Store 0.9.29)
body:
iPhone tethering: a switch that leaves a plugged-in iPhone to the car, so its USB music plays. Releases **mgu-uplink 0.7.7**, **mgu-updater 0.8.32** and **robertn_store 0.9.29**.

## Why

Once an iPhone trusts the unit, the uplink takes it from the media daemon every time it is plugged in. It keeps the phone even with Personal Hotspot off: the stall check in `iphone.go` skips a phone whose carrier reads off, so the link stays up and only notes `Personal Hotspot is off`. The phone is a network device the whole time, so its USB music never comes back. The only ways out were resetting the phone's trust (Reset Location & Privacy) and tapping Don't Trust on every plug-in, or removing the uplink.

## What changes

**mgu-uplink 0.7.7**
- A new setting, `iphone = on|off` (`on` shipped). It is kept in `settings_conf` by the new request `{"op": "iphone", "on": false}`. `settings_conf` is read leniently, so a rollback skips the line.
- Off: the scan lists no iPhone, so it stays the media daemon's.
- An iPhone the uplink holds, or is still taking, when the setting goes off is handed back within 5 s. Its link, or the grab's `checkPreferred`, ends with `errIPhoneOff`, and the link's close reauthorizes the device, so the media daemon reclaims it. That end does not count as a failed open.
- `status.json` adds `iphone` with `uplink = auto`. The start log line names it.
- `preferEvery` is now a var, so the test can shorten it.

**mgu-updater 0.8.32**
- `{"op":"uplink-iphone","on":true|false}` (privileged) is relayed as the uplink's `iphone`.

**robertn_store 0.9.29**
- The preferred connection's page has **iPhone tethering**, a switch below the four groups, with `Stops the iPhone's USB music` under it.
- It shows only with an uplink that reports `iphone`, and sends `uplink-iphone`.
- The Store requires mgu-updater 0.8.32.
- The words are in every language. The CJK phrasings use only characters the atlases already hold, so the fonts are not baked again.

## Tests

- **mgu-uplink:** `go vet` and `go test ./...` pass in `golang:1.22`. New tests:
  - `TestIPhoneSwitchedOff`: no candidate while off; a link on an iPhone ends with `errIPhoneOff` once switched off.
  - `TestIPhoneSetting`: the shipped value, `settings_conf`, and a bad value skipped.
  - `TestControlRequests` adds the request, `settings_conf` and `status.json`.
- **mgu-updater:** `test/run.sh` (Node 8.16.2 in Docker) passes. The uplink test covers the relay and refusing a non-boolean `on`.
- **robertn_store:** the release build chain passes: build, i18n, fit, view, rhmi, qr, speller, screens, and store on ID7 and ID8. The new checks cover the row and its state, no row with an older uplink, and a tap sending `uplink-iphone`.

**Not done:** I haven't run the emulator, and there's no gate record for 0.9.29. Both are still to do before publishing. It hasn't been tried in a car yet either.

title: Feature request: user-configurable mirrors for update sources
body:
Hi Robert,

Thank you for your work on this project! There are many enthusiastic users in mainland China, and I'd like to help make the project easier to use here while contributing back.

Access to GitHub and its download hosts can sometimes be unreliable, especially when the head unit connects through a phone hotspot. Thank you for adding proxy support — it helps, but having a reachable proxy available to the head unit can still require extra setup.

Would you be open to extending the existing source configuration so users can provide their own mirrors?

I'm not asking for any regional mirror to be bundled, endorsed or maintained by the project. Official GitHub sources would remain the default. The idea is simply to let users:

- Configure an HTTPS catalog mirror for an official source, including the Store's own source.
- Choose whether to fall back to the official source when the mirror is unavailable, avoiding repeated requests to hosts they cannot reach.

Existing package integrity checks and dependency handling should remain in place.

I've prepared a mirror for users in mainland China and would be happy to take on implementation, testing and maintenance of this feature, with a PR following your preferred design. Maintaining the mirror service itself would remain my responsibility.

Does this direction fit the project? Would you prefer extending the existing HTTPS source support, or a different approach?

I'd appreciate your guidance before starting the implementation. Thanks!

title: mgu-render 0.6.13: the touch divert rule goes to nft in a file and counts only when its table is there
body:
**Problem.** On a G20 (iDrive 7, MainApp 8.2.0, firmware J18_21w19.2-1-5, nftables v0.7) touch never reaches the Store. mgu-render 0.6.12 hands the divert rule to `nft -f -`, and this nft reads `-` as a file name:

```
# echo 'table ip x' | nft -f - ; echo "exit=$?"
internal:0:0-0: Error: Could not open file "-": No such file or directory
exit=0
```

So the journal says `touch: diverted (an app claims an area)` while `nft list tables` shows only `ip filter` / `ip6 filter`, and every touch stays with the HMI.

**Change.**
- `touch.c`: the script is written to `/tmp/mgu-render-nft-XXXXXX` and loaded with `nft -f <file>`.
- A load counts only when `nft list table ip mgu_render` finds the table afterwards. Otherwise the journal says `touch: loading the nft rule failed, touch stays the HMI's` and the load is tried again after 5 s (the existing retry).
- `test_touch.c`: the stand-in nft reads the file it is given. New checks: every script goes to nft in a file, and a load whose table is not there counts as failed.
- mgu-render 0.6.13, CHANGELOG.

This is the change in #132 (reported there on MainApp 6.5.5), on top of 0.6.12, plus a test for the table check: #132 is based on 0.6.11 and now conflicts with main in `component.json` / `CHANGELOG.md`. Take whichever suits you and close the other. #186 (touch works everywhere except in the Store) looks like the same symptom.

**Tested.**
- `make test`: everything passes (`test_touch: 22 checks, 0 failed`). With 0.6.12's `touch.c` the new checks fail (2 of 22).
- `make check-target`: OK, glibc up to 2.17.
- On the car (nft v0.7): a script of the same shape, written to a file under /tmp, loads (exit 0) and its table is listed; `nft list table` exits 0 while the table is there and 1 once it is deleted.
- Not yet run: the patched binary on the car, and the emulator.

title: Turn source repositories on and off, Sources drop-down, Show/Apps/Tools buttons
body:
### What and why
Makes it easier to find and debug your own tools by hiding or showing everything a repo provides.

**mgu-updater 0.8.32**
- New privileged request `source-enable` (`{ id, enable }` or `{ all: true, enable }`). A source that is off stays in `sources.json` (`disabled: true`) with its kept catalog, is not read, and none of its components are listed. What it installed stays installed.
- The state reports `disabled` and status `disabled`. Turning a source on lists its kept catalog and reads the source only when it has none; the next check reads it again. The Store's own source can't be turned off.

**Store 0.9.29** (requires updater 0.8.28; without updater 0.8.32 there is no switch)
- Settings, Sources: a switch on each source except the Store's own and a stick; the switch shows at once.
- Store tab: a Sources drop-down (`Sources num of selected/all`) with a checkbox per source, Select all and Uncheck all.
- Store tab: Show (each press: all, installed, not installed) and Apps and Tools buttons (each on or off) replace the All/Apps/Tools tabs. On iDrive 7 these sit in a row above the tiles, because the header had no room for 32 languages (`test_fit`).
- Fix: an app page's notes (why it can't be installed, restart pending, for another head unit) wrap over several lines instead of one cut line.

### Updates in any order
Store 0.9.29 requires updater 0.8.28 (`release.json`, unchanged). A Store without updater 0.8.32 just shows no switch; the new updater works with the old Store.

### Merged with main
Merged `main` (Store 0.9.28, updater 0.8.31) into this branch and renumbered above it: Store 0.9.25 → 0.9.29, updater 0.8.28 → 0.8.32. The Store package folder is `main`'s 0.9.28 tree with this PR's changes and changelog entry.

### Tested
- Store: `test_view`, `test_screens` (3 boxes), `test_store` (iDrive 7 and 8), `test_i18n` (32 languages), `test_fit`, `test_rhmi`, `test_qr`, `test_speller` all pass again after the merge with main.
- Updater: `source-enable` checked with a standalone script and new cases in `test_updater.js`; the updater test suite passes on Node 8 after the merge.
- On a car: iDrive 7, running the same code as a variant app (before the merge, as Store 2 0.9.27 with updater 0.8.29). **The merged Store 0.9.29 and updater 0.8.32 have not been run on a car yet.**

### Please check
- The translations of `Not installed`, `Disabled`, `Select all`, `Uncheck all` and `Sources {0}/{1}` are mine for 31 languages. They need a native read. Japanese uses 未インストール and 選択をクリア because the baked font lacks some kanji.
- Where to look: `native/mgu-updater/js/updater.js` (`sourceEnable`), `store_ui.js`, `store.js` (`_enableSource`), and `store_compact.js` / `am_screens.js` for the layouts. `locales.js`, the locale JSON files and `rhmiData` are generated.

title: Head unit boot-loops after first-install on firmware 030.016 (iDrive 7) — home screen comes up, then reboots; no network
body:
After running deploy/mgu-install.js first-install and accepting the reboot, the head unit now boot-loops: the home screen comes up for a few seconds, then the unit reboots, repeatedly. The MGU no longer brings up its network (MGU IP 0.0.0.0, port 22 closed), so I can't SSH in to inspect. The unit is still reachable over ENET diagnostics (gateway found, VIN and SVK read fine), and the reversing camera still works.

I'd appreciate help identifying which install-time change is blocking boot and how to revert it over ENET, since SSH is currently unavailable.

Head unit
iDrive 7 (MGU), firmware BMW MGU J18_21w19.2-1-5 mgu-high
SVK: BTLD 030.016.006, SWFL 030.016.002, CAFD 00003E52_008.010.128
VIN: (will provide privately if needed)
What I did, in order
Enabled root SSH with cauliflowermossgrape/idrive7-8-ssh-root while the unit was on an older level (018.014). enable --persist succeeded, B7F8E5 cleared, SSH worked (verified uid=0(root)), survived a reboot.
Ran node mgu-install.js first-install --identity <key> --host <ip>. It installed app-privacy 1.7.1, mgu-deploy 0.7.14, mgu-python 1.0.2, mgu-updater 0.8.19, robertn_store 0.9.16, mgu-render 0.6.9, mgu-uplink 0.7.3, then asked to restart the head unit. I answered y.
At some point the unit's software updated itself to 030.016 (BTLD 030.016.006 / SWFL 030.016.002). Store became 0.9.17, mgu-deploy 0.7.15, and state.json listed many extra apps (car_vitals, live_adjustments, iteriodev-*, doom, etc.) that I did not knowingly install.
After that, the home screen started coming up briefly and then rebooting in a loop.
Current state (over ENET diagnostics)
status (from idrive7-8-ssh-root): gateway 169.254.24.46 found, VIN read OK, full SVK read OK, but MGU IP: 0.0.0.0 / netmask 255.255.255.255, port 22 not open, DTC B7F8E5 present, debug/SSH-open state ON.
Ping to the old MGU IP times out.
Reversing camera works when in reverse.
Home screen (Media/Radio, clock, Communication) renders for a few seconds each cycle, then the screen goes dark and the unit reboots.
What I already tried
Restored the head unit coding from an ESYS backup (same car, matching level). First attempt wrote cafd_00003e52-008_010_130 and finished with warnings (and the loop continued); a second write landed cafd_00003e52-008_010_128 and finished cleanly. The boot loop persists either way.
Let the unit sit powered-down for 20+ minutes between attempts. No change.
What I think is involved (not sure)

The installer created/changed boot-time units and a bind mount, which I suspect is blocking boot now that the firmware moved to 030.016:

mgu-app-fallback.service bind-mounts /var/opt/mgu-deploy/main.js over /usr/lib/oap-mainapp/src/main.bundle.js. Note: that main.js was dated 2021-04-12 and did not look rebuilt for the new firmware.
Overrides created under /etc/systemd/system: hmi.service.wants, hmi.service.d, display-bridge.socket.d, display-bridge.service.d, display-bridge-hmi.service.d, var-opt-ro.service.d, carplay.service.d.
app-privacy patched MainApp 8.2.0.
Questions
Is there a safe way, over ENET only (no SSH), to disable mgu-app-fallback and the fallback bind mount so the unit boots stock?
Does first-install on 030.016 need a rebuilt main.js, and could the stale 2021 main.js bind-mounted over MainApp cause this loop?
Is the right recovery to re-flash the debug image and restore coding, or is there a lighter revert?

title: app-privacy 1.8.0: BMW apps on a never-start list don't start (MainApp 8.3.2)
body:
MainApp starts every provisioned BMW app as its provisioning says: at boot, from the backend, from autostart and last-used restore. There's no way to keep one you never use from starting, and removing it isn't an option because the backend puts it back.

This adds an optional list, `/var/opt/public/oap/oap_12201/data/never-start-apps.json`, a JSON array of appIds, the same shape as `local-only-apps.json`. A BMW app listed there:

- is not startable: `App._isStartable` returns false for it, which every start path asks (tile, widgets, voice, backend, other apps, crash recovery, autostart, last-used restore). Its tile and voice command stay listed, using them does nothing;
- runs as start type `manually` whatever its provisioning says, so the autostart queue doesn't wait on it;
- stays out of the config-state queue.

Its provisioning isn't changed, so emptying the file restores the stock behaviour at the next MainApp start.

Safety:
- `x_call`, `ts_diagnostic_service`, `privacy_manager` and `oap-cdc-2018` are never matched, even if listed.
- A missing, unreadable or invalid file means every app starts as provisioned.
- Nothing ships a list and nothing writes the file. Without it, nothing changes. A Store setting to edit it could come later if you want one; I didn't add UI here.
- Only MainApp 8.3.2 gets the four `never-start-*` edits, and they're optional. 8.2.10, 8.1.1, 6.5.5 and MainApp-21 are patched exactly as in 1.7.1. 1.7.1's set is kept in `EARLIER_PATCH_SETS`, so a bundle patched by 1.7.1 is recognised and upgraded by `apply`.

Tests
- `sh native/app-privacy/test/run.sh`: 77/77 pass (Node 8.16.2). New cases: the helper (only listed apps, never a denied one, never on a bad file), start type `manually` with provisioning untouched, out of the config-state queue, not startable while others vote as before, and earlier releases' sets carry no never-start edit.
- I don't have a decoded 8.3.2 here, so `PATCHED_SHA256.current.main` is `null` and the reference-firmware test skips that one compare. Could you record the 1.8.0 `main.js` hash from your firmware run?
- Tested on my car (iDrive 7, MainApp 8.3.2-pr-847.1): 1.8.0 installed, `check` reports `patched` with all six never-start edits applied. `never-start-apps.json` holds `["cmusic"]`, which is provisioned `autostart` by the backend. After a full restart (1h15 uptime) no process runs under cmusic's uid, its `configStateQueueIndex` is null, and the other 13 apps start as usual.

Update order: app-privacy only, no `requires`.

Not run: `tools/emu-gate`, I don't have the emulator.

title: mgu-updater 0.8.22: JustAnotherPU/mgu-apps, moonride and waze-hud as default sources, on their releases
body:
Adds three of my repos as default sources, the same way as idrive-apps (#79) and car-apps (#86):

- listed in `updater.conf` `default_sources` (`JustAnotherPU/mgu-apps:releases JustAnotherPU/moonride:releases JustAnotherPU/waze-hud:releases`);
- seeded by the installers (`deploy/sources.json` and `SOURCES` in `deploy/mgu-install.js`, ids `mgu-apps`, `moonride`, `waze-hud`);
- added once at the first start of 0.8.22, unless a source of that repo is already there;
- removable, and not added again once removed.

What they provide (all public, every component `mguHmi: ["ID7"]`, so nothing is offered on iDrive 8):

- [mgu-apps](https://github.com/JustAnotherPU/mgu-apps): iDrive Monitor (`jap_sysmon`, CPU, memory and graphics load with a pop-up when the unit runs short), and two shared tools: Node.js 22 (`jap-node22`) and Tailscale (`jap-tailscale`, the tailnet through a local SOCKS5 proxy). MIT; the Tailscale tool's scripts are GPL-3.0-or-later.
- [moonride](https://github.com/JustAnotherPU/moonride): Moonride, a Moonlight game streaming client for the centre screen (1920x720, 60 fps) with the sound on the car's speakers. It requires `jap-node22` from mgu-apps, which is why mgu-apps is in the list too. GPL-3.0-or-later.
- [waze-hud](https://github.com/JustAnotherPU/waze-hud): Waze HUD, derived from idrive-apps' waze-on-cluster. It sends Waze's next turn to BMW's own HUD arrows and shows the map on the cluster, using your cluster-render from idrive-apps. If waze-on-cluster is installed it stays dormant and offers a pop-up to remove the other one. GPL-3.0-or-later.

**Channel: releases.** Each repo has a `catalog` release, so the updater reads its `catalog.json` without the API. All three `releases/download/catalog/catalog.json` URLs resolve without a token.

**Docs:** README, deploy/README.md and the updater README list the sources. Version 0.8.22 with its changelog entry.

Tests
- `sh native/mgu-updater/test/run.sh`: 528 passed, 0 failed.
- `sh deploy/test/run.sh`: 1023/1023, including "the installers seed the updater's default sources" and "mgu-install: seeds the same sources as deploy/hu".
- I haven't yet installed these apps from these sources through the Store on a car.

Update order: updater only, no `requires`.

Not run: `tools/emu-gate`, I don't have the emulator.

title: mgu-python 1.0.3: the standard library's .pyc in the zip, so the unit doesn't compile it at every start
body:
`lib/python312.zip` only has `.py` files. Python can't write `.pyc` into a zip, so every process on the unit compiles each stdlib module it imports, every time. On the head unit's Atom that's about 4 s for the ~250 modules a typical script pulls in. On my car (iDrive 7), a script that imports yt-dlp took 5.1 s to import; with the `.pyc` in the zip it took 1.2 s.

What changed in `build.js`:

- After staging the stdlib, it runs `compileall -b --invalidation-mode unchecked-hash` on the files that go into the zip, and adds each `.pyc` next to its `.py`. That's the legacy layout zipimport reads. Unchecked hash because zip members have no mtime to compare.
- That needs a Python 3.12 on the build machine: `$PY312`, else `uv python find 3.12`, else `python3.12` on `PATH`. Without one, the build stops and says so.

The artifact goes from about 14 MB to 18 MB (36 MB installed). The README and `release/README.md` say so. The release README also notes that the host Python 3.12 is a second outside input, like Node's zlib: another 3.12.x release can write different bytecode, so releases are best built with the same 3.12.x.

Tests
- `release.js check mgu-python` is reproducible (built twice, same 18012752 bytes) with a host Python 3.12.14.
- The built zip has 505 `.py` and 505 `.pyc`.
- Installed on my car since November 3; the import times above are from there.

Update order: mgu-python only, no `requires`. Nothing that uses it changes.

Not run: `tools/emu-gate`, I don't have the emulator.

title: mgu-render 0.6.12: the foreground gate retries an instance that failed and rereads one that becomes available
body:
On my car (iDrive 7), after an iDrive start, the idrive7-apps kit apps sometimes never went full screen. They drew inside the HMI's page, with the HMI's button bar under them. One drive Redline stayed like that the whole way.

The foreground gate builds one SOME/IP proxy per `RemoteHmiApplication` instance once, at start. While the HMI is still starting, some of those proxies fail. A failed instance was never watched again until the renderer restarted, so an app the HMI later showed there was never "in front", and the kit drew it in the HMI's page.

What changed in `js/foreground_gate.js`:

1. An instance whose proxy fails is tried again every 5 s until it works. The first failure is logged, and once it works: `<instance>: watched after N retries`.
2. When an instance becomes available, its `applicationStack` is read again. A stack set before then is not always sent to us.

Nothing else changes: instances that work at the first try behave as before.

Tests
- `make test` in `native/mgu-render`: 0 failed, 28 replays identical.
- New `test/test_gate_watch.js` (run by `make test`) uses a mock SOME/IP: one instance fails twice and then works, another never sends its stack and is read when it becomes available. On main the first instance is never watched, so the test fails there.
- Installed on my car since November 3. I haven't yet confirmed the after-iDrive-start case on a drive (a "watched after N retries" line in the journal with the kit apps going full screen).

Update order: renderer only, no `requires`.

Not run: `tools/emu-gate`, I don't have the emulator.

title: mgu-render 0.6.9 beside idrive7-renderd: after mgu-render restarts, idrive7-apps' apps lose the iDrive knob until a head-unit restart
body:
**Car:** 2021 X5 M50i (G05, US), iDrive 7. mgu-render **0.6.9** (Store), idrive7-renderd 2.1.10
and mgu-inputgate 1.0.0 (loaded in HmiMain3D) from idrive7-apps. The app is an idrive7-apps kit
app (my own, FuelBlend) on idrive7-renderd's socket.

**What happened:** the knob stopped working in the kit app (touch still worked). From then on,
every connection to idrive7-renderd got READY with `"controller": false`, until a head-unit
restart:

```
06:43:38 renderd: connected, screen 1920x720, mgu-render/1 {"touch":true,"controller":true,"frontGate":true}
06:53:29 renderd: connected, screen 1920x720, mgu-render/1 {"touch":true,"controller":false,"frontGate":true}
... "controller":false at 06:59, 07:05, 07:20 and 07:23
```

`mgu-render.service` started at **06:52:20 UTC** (systemctl `start_time`), a minute before the
first `false`. idrive7-renderd had started at about 06:42. I think the Store's restart was an
update, but I didn't log that.

**How I read it:** the README's "Beside other renderers > Controller" says mgu-render binds
`@mgu-renderd-ccu` only while one of its apps holds GRAB. idrive7-renderd (the same engine)
offers `controller` in READY only while that socket is free or its own, and the kit only grabs
when READY offered it. So `false` on every connection for 30 minutes means something held
`@mgu-renderd-ccu` that whole time. mgu-render, right after its restart, is the likely one: a
Store app still holding GRAB while not in front, or counted as shown after the restart. **That's
inferred.** I didn't catch who had the socket, and I didn't have mgu-render's journal from that
time.

The kit side (it checks READY once per connection and never asks again) is
cauliflowermossgrape/idrive7-apps#81.

**Possible fixes on this side:**
1. Make sure the socket is released whenever no mgu-render app is in front, including right after
   a restart.
2. Log when mgu-render binds and releases `@mgu-renderd-ccu` and for which app, if
   `controller: held for an app` / `back to the HMI` don't already cover it.

**To pin it down next time** (read-only, while the knob is gone):

```sh
grep mgu-renderd-ccu /proc/net/unix
I=<inode>; for p in /proc/[0-9]*; do ls -l $p/fd 2>/dev/null | grep -q "socket:\[$I\]" && echo "$p $(cat $p/comm)"; done
journalctl -u mgu-render.service | grep 'controller:'
```

**Workaround:** restart the head unit.

(Not related: the `the HMI was touched - closed` lines from header-tab taps on 0.6.9 are the
title-strip `touch_area` issue that 0.6.11 fixes.)

title: Request: add aurelmarius/bmw-games as a default source
body:
Hi Robert,

Thanks for mgu-store, it's become the easiest way to get apps onto the car.

I'd like to ask whether you'd consider adding my games repository to the Store's default sources, next to idrive7-apps, idrive-apps and car-apps:

**https://github.com/aurelmarius/bmw-games** (Releases layout, iDrive 7)

It has eight games and more to come, all built with the idrive7-apps kit, all drawn by mgu-render at 60 fps (with the HMI-image fallback when the renderer isn't there), playable with the iDrive controller or the touchscreen, and all **parked only** (they pause above 3 km/h and can't be started while driving).

Also, a small idea, as more apps and games show up for the head unit:
Today the Store page lists every app and tool from every source together. With a few sources added, the games end up mixed with the car apps (gauges, DTC scanners, cost calculators...), and a game is easy to miss, or in the way when you're after a tool.

**Proposal:** an optional category per app, that the Store shows as a filter (or a section) on its Store page:

- `"category": "games"` on a component in `catalog.json` (and/or `mguCategory` in `package.json`, for the other layouts)
- a few fixed values to start with, e.g. `games`, `vehicle` (gauges, diagnostics, data), `media`, `tools` — anything without one stays where it is today, so nothing changes for existing sources
- on the Store page: **All · Games · …** tabs or chips at the top, only the ones that have something in them

Since games are parked-only by nature, the category could also let the Store show a small "parked only" note on their page, but that's a nice-to-have.

title: Stock BMW apps reinstalled from firmware (4 missing) after back-to-back Store installs, MainApp 8.2.8
body:
**Unit:** iDrive 7, G30 LCI, firmware K18_21w45.4-1-3, MainApp 8.2.8. mgu-deploy 0.7.11, app-privacy 1.7.1, mgu-updater 0.8.14.

**What happened:** On 2026-11-02 between 09:55 and 10:05 UTC I installed several apps from the Store one after another (Redline, Fault Scanner, Service, the Waze on cluster app), plus the mgu-updater 0.8.14 update (backup `20261102T100159222Z-install`). At 10:04–10:05 several stock BMW apps were reinstalled from the firmware's preinstalled packages, with new uids and older versions, and four disappeared:

| app | before (status 2026-10-31) | after |
|---|---|---|
| x_call | 4.84.32, uid 12229 | 4.25.3, uid 12243 |
| ts_diagnostic_service | 4.31.17, uid 12205 | 4.20.2, uid 12242 |
| ts_battery_guard | 4.31.5, uid 12207 | 4.22.1, uid 12241 |
| trigger_service | 2.18.19, uid 12224 | 2.16.0, uid 12240 |
| ts_rsu_report | 4.27.2, uid 12221 | missing |
| ts_service_partner | 4.33.10, uid 12210 | missing |
| ts_servicecall | 4.28.14, uid 12216 | missing |
| ts_workshop_detection | 4.0.16, uid 12230 | missing |

**What's still on the unit:**
- All eight old folders are intact (`/var/opt/public/oap/oap_<uid>/` with `source`, `data`, `kvs`, `security`, `someipInterfaces`), at the versions above.
- In `oap_12201/data/apps/`, the four reinstalled apps' JSONs were rewritten at 10:04–10:05 (e.g. `x_call.json` now has `userId: 12243`); the four missing apps have no JSON.
- `oap_12236`–`oap_12239` were created in the same window and no app in `status` uses them.
- The mgu-deploy backups from before 10:04 don't hold the app registry, so the old JSONs are gone.

**Side effect:** since then adding a driver profile in iDrive fails ("An error occurred, try again later"). Remote services from the My BMW app still work.

**Questions:**
1. Is there a safe way to point the registry back at the old folders, or to reinstall these apps from their old `source` folders with mgu-deploy?
2. Could the Store/updater pace back-to-back installs and updates so the manager can't hit oapcontroller's third-crash wipe?

I have root SSH and can run any read-only diagnostics or test a fix.

title: Page changes without a black box: mgu-render 0.6.11 bridges the HMI's page change with a layer of its own, robertn_store 0.9.17 asks for it

**Change.**
- mgu-render 0.6.11: on the app's `X_BRIDGE 1`, the renderer shows the app's frames on a layer of its own over exactly the box, for `embed_bridge_ms` (400).

  - `X_BRIDGE 0` (an HMI popup, menu or HOME)
  - the app no longer being in front
  - a camera showing
  - the app hiding or disconnecting

title: mgu-render 0.6.11: the foreground gate also looks for the RemoteHmiApplication description in the src-gen folders of the packages under /usr/lib
body:
**Problem.** MainApp 6.5.5 (a single bundle) keeps the `RemoteHmiApplication` description in its own package's `src-gen` folder, not in `oap-mainapp`. The gate found none of the known files.

**Change.**
- `findInterface` checks the known files first. Then it checks any `de_bmw_infotainment_hmi_remote[2]_RemoteHmiApplication[2].json` in the `src-gen` folder of each package under `/usr/lib` (two levels deep). Last come the apps' `someipInterfaces` copies.
- One more case in `test_gate.js`.

**Tested.** `test_gate.js` (9 checks). On the car: the gate reported apps in front after the fix.

title: mgu-render 0.6.11: the touch divert rule goes to nft in a file and counts only when its table is there
body:
**Problem.** On some iDrive 7 cars (seen with MainApp 6.5.5) `nft -f -` cannot read a script from stdin. The renderer logged `touch: diverted`, but the `mgu_render` table was never there, so no touch reached the Store or the apps. Seen in `nft list tables` on the car: only `ip filter` / `ip6 filter` while an app was shown.

**Change.**
- `touch.c`: the script is written to `/tmp/mgu-render-nft-XXXXXX` and loaded with `nft -f <file>`.
- After a load, `nft list table ip mgu_render` must succeed, or the load counts as failed (logged, retried after 5 s).
- `test_touch.c`: the fake nft reads the file it is given.

**Tested.** `test_touch` (19 checks); the rule file loads with a real nft in a network namespace. On the car: touch reached the apps after the fix.

body:

title: iDrive 7 MainApp 7.1.2 (firmware G_20w28.3): Store never installed (600 s, no registry entry); restore stock failed once after the rollback
body:
Hi! Report from an iDrive 7 head unit on 2020 firmware. I understand MainApp 7.x is outside what the deploy tool and app-privacy target (README: 8.1.1 / 8.3.2), so this is mostly information, plus one rollback/restore bug that may matter on supported units too.

## Head unit
- BMW 320i G20 (2020/2021), iDrive 7 (MGU ID7)
- Firmware: `BMW MGU G_20w28.3-1-2 mgu-high`; SVK `BTLD 00003F36_014.009.005`, SWFL `014.009.002`
- MainApp: **7.1.2**; Kernel 4.14.147-apl, BusyBox 1.27.2
- Root SSH via idrive7-8-ssh-root (`flash --persist`), over ENET from Windows 11, Node 18+

## 1. Store install never completes
`node mgu-install.js first-install --identity <key> --host 169.254.93.96`, twice (the second after a full power-down, with mgu-updater 0.8.10):

```
built robertn_store 0.9.14 from its source package (625 modules, oap-sdk from ts_diagnostic_service@4.20.0.tgz:javascript/app.js, ...)
fallback_build: anchors for our apps first in the install queue not found exactly once; the copy leaves the queue as it is
installing tool app-privacy 1.6.0 ... installed   (app-privacy: patched (applied now))
installing tool mgu-deploy 0.7.0 / mgu-python 1.0.2 / mgu-updater 0.8.9 ... installed
installing app robertn_store 0.9.14
keychain wait of MainApp's installs: 115 s ...
provisioning fallback turned on
installing robertn_store through a bounce: its main.js or AppManagement.js was written after it started
bouncing the app manager node child (pid 4912)
app manager respawned (pid 5617)
rolling back robertn_store 0.9.14 from /var/opt/mgu-deploy/backups/20261031T154632452Z-install
robertn_store 0.9.14 failed: app manager did not install robertn_store 0.9.14 within 600s (no registry entry)
```

What I found in MainApp 7.1.2's `main.js`:
- The two mandatory fallback anchors and the in-place hook anchor are found; `QUEUE_ANCHOR` is found too, but there is **no `queuedRecursiveRetry` / `AppManagementController`** (so no `CONTROLLER_ANCHOR`).
- Installs from provisioning go through `MainApp._provisioningDataChanged` → `_triggerAppInstallationIfNeeded(list, "install")`, queued on `MainApp._operationPromise` behind the start-up forced-update pass (`_triggerAppInstallationIfNeeded(getAllAppIdsWhichNeedsAnUpdate(), "update")`). It installs **sequentially** (`Promise.mapSeries`) in `installable_apps` order and retries network failures after `networkErrorInstallationRetryTimeout * 2^n`. The fallback appends our apps at the **end** of `installable_apps` (`__haveList.concat(__missing)`), so the Store waits behind every BMW install/update attempt. I suspect that's why it never got a registry entry within 600 s, but I couldn't see MainApp's DLT log to confirm.
- During the wait, `mgu-deploy.sh status` showed `fallback: active (bind-mounted true, apps robertn_store)`, MainApp's node child up (uid 12201), and the stock apps respawned normally.

## 2. Bug: rollback left main.js bound to a deleted copy, then `restore stock` failed once
After the second failed install's rollback, `/proc/mounts` still showed `/usr/lib/oap-mainapp/src/main.js` bind-mounted from `/dev/mmcblk0p10`, while the fallback copy `/var/opt/mgu-deploy/main.js` was gone. `mgu-deploy.sh restore stock --yes` then printed:

```
app-privacy: unpatched (reverted now)
app-privacy (stock main.js under the fallback copy): unpatched (reverted now)
restore failed, rolling back from /var/opt/mgu-deploy/backups/20261031T173032780Z-restore
mgu-deploy: mount --bind /var/opt/mgu-deploy/main.js /usr/lib/oap-mainapp/src/main.js exited 32: mount: ... special device /var/opt/mgu-deploy/main.js does not exist.
```

It looks like `privacyRevert()`'s `finally` re-binds `FALLBACK_COPY` without checking it exists. After that run, main.js was unbound and the fallback unit absent. A second `restore stock --yes` succeeded (`restored from stock`), and main.js's sha256 matched the stock snapshot's record (`a9439f01…210e`).

## 3. Leftover after restore
`12225=robertn_store` stayed in `/var/opt/public/oap/oap_12201/security/uids.txt` with no registry entry. That matches the documented "manager-side records are not removed", but it made idrive7-apps' installer refuse to start (`inconsistent: robertn_store in uids.txt has no registry entry`) until I removed the line.

## Afterwards
idrive7-apps' own installer (direct registration, no MainApp install queue) installed 8 apps fine on this unit, and its renderer works with two tweaks. Details in robertnisipeanu/idrive-apps#8: the foreground gate interface is at `/usr/lib/oap-mainapp/src-gen/someip/` on 7.1.2, and touch routing had to be turned off (`touch=0`).
